To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

palladium-complex-catalyzed intermolecular oxidative amination with secondary amines was successfully achieved using molecular oxygen, and that oxidative amination of anilines with alkenes was also achieved with molecular oxygen as the oxidant, producing N-alkenyl anilines in a highly regio- and stereoselective manner.

palladium-catalysed oxidative amination of olefins with amines using molecular oxygen as a terminal oxidant is an environmentally benign method to produce allylic aminates and enamines in high selectivities and high yields.

palladium-complexes are effective catalysts for the intermolecular oxidative amination reaction of alkenes, using molecular oxygen and amines as terminal oxidants, leading to allylamines, enamines and anilines in good yields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel Pd-catalysts for the intermolecular oxidative amination reaction of alkenes using molecular oxygen.

the development of a new synthetic method of amination of aliphatic alkenes with various amines, using molecular oxygen, which can be regarded as an alternative to the use of stoichiometric amounts of oxidants.
the development of novel palladium-catalytic methods, which enable the oxidative amination of unactivated alkenes with primary and secondary anilines under molecular oxygen as the oxidant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
palladium-catalysed oxidative amination of olefins with amines, using molecular oxygen, is one of the most promising methods for the preparation of allylic and N-alkenyl aniline derivatives.
the Pd-catalytic oxidative amination of olefins with anilines is a powerful method for the preparation of N-arylated allylamines and N-arylated enamines.
the oxidative amination of simple olefins with anilines using molecular oxygen is a powerful and efficient method for the synthesis of (Z)-N-(2-alkenyl)anilines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxidative amination of terminal alkenes with primary amines, using molecular oxygen, is an effective method for the synthesis of allylamine derivatives.
the oxidative amination of anilines as a primary amine was achieved using molecular dioxygen as the terminal oxidand.
the palladium-catalysed oxidative amination of simple olefins with anilines, using molecular oxygen, can provide a variety of N-alkenyl anilines in good to excellent yields with good selectivities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pd-catalysis is a powerful tool for the synthesis of N-alkenyl compounds, and the use of molecular oxygen as the oxidant is an attractive and environmentally friendly method.
palladium-catalysts combined with co-catalysts are effective for oxidative amination of unactivated alkenes with molecular oxygen as the oxidant.

palladium catalysts combined with co-catalysts can induce oxidative amination of various alkenes with primary and secondary amines under dioxygen, producing allylic aminates and enamines in high yields and with excellent selectivities.
